steps.title: NAG restores negative prompts at guidance 1 on the Wan student, written from its paper into the conditioned diffusion block's cross-attention
steps.rationale:
The Wan student runs at guidance 1, so it honours no negative prompt. NAG (Chen et al., arXiv 2505.21179, read 2026-11-11) guides in attention space at no extra model pass: in each cross-attention, the image tokens' query attends to the prompt's keys and values (Z+) and to the negative prompt's (Z-); Eq. 7 extrapolates Z~ = Z+ + phi (Z+ - Z-); Eq. 8 takes each token's L1 ratio R = |Z~|_1 / |Z+|_1 over the feature dimension; Eq. 9 clips it, Z^ = min(R, tau) / R Z~; Eq. 10 blends, Z = alpha Z^ + (1 - alpha) Z+. It sits on the attention output, before the output projection (Eq. 4 and the paper's pseudocode). Table 5 gives Wan2.1 phi 4, tau 2.5, alpha 0.25. Its reported gains: ImageReward 1.029 to 1.099 on Flux-Schnell, at 43 to 87% more time.

The conditioned diffusion block (internal/model) gains NAG on its cross-attention, from the graph builder's operations (ReLU for the absolute value, SumRows, Divide, Clamp, Multiply), fed the negative prompt's per-block keys and values; the Wan student's request names a nag preset and a negative prompt, whose context is projected once as the prompt's is.

Check: TestNAGAppliesANegativePromptAtGuidanceOne, in internal/model (a block with NAG, evaluated by the reference backend on small weights, against Eqs. 7 to 10 written out in the test, and the block without a negative context unchanged) and internal/latentvideo (the student with the nag preset and a negative prompt draws another clip than without one, at the passes it ran before).

Serves: held-out-quality; a capability the distilled models lack.
Disappears: nothing.
Evidence: the preset's reading is guidance-ops/preset-readings'.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: NAG restores negative prompts on Krea-2-Turbo, once the paper's reading of joint attention is recorded
steps.rationale:
Krea-2-Turbo runs without guidance, so it honours no negative prompt, and raising guidance over-cooks it. NAG (arXiv 2505.21179) is defined on an attention output Z = Softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V, its Eqs. 7 to 10 given in guidance-ops/nag-wan, and the paper says it adds computation to cross-attention layers or MM-DiT blocks, but not how a negative prompt enters joint attention: whether the text tokens run as a second stream through every block, and whether the image tokens are shared. Krea2 runs its text and image tokens as one co-attention sequence through all 28 blocks, so that choice decides the work and the cost. Krea's published settings are phi 4.0, tau 2.5, alpha 0.25.

Before work: settle from the paper, its appendix and its supplementary material (not code) how Z- is formed in joint attention, and record the reading as a note here; a choice the paper does not make is the owner's, asked with the cost of each way.

Check: TestNAGAppliesANegativePromptAtGuidanceOne in internal/latentimage: Krea with the nag preset and a negative prompt draws another picture than without one, and with no negative prompt the picture it drew before.

steps.title: bong_tangent, beta57 and a request's own sigma list are named schedules, bong_tangent's sigmas equal to the recorded ones at 8 and 50 steps and at denoise 0.72
steps.rationale:
The owner decided on 2026-11-05 that bong_tangent becomes a named schedule. It is built from its formula, not translated from RES4LYF's Python: two arctangent segments, from 1.0 to 0.5 and from 0.5 to 0.0, joined near the step pivot; pivots 0.6 and slopes 0.2, the slopes scaled by steps / 40; steps + 2 points with the joining point counted once; no flow shift, so MOSS's shift of 5 does not apply. Its provenance note names RES4LYF and its licence, AGPL-3.0 with a clause against use in a commercial AI image service without the author's licence, which binds overgo if it is ever offered as such a service. beta57 is the beta schedule at alpha 0.5, beta 0.7, from its paper. A request may carry its own sigmas, as ComfyUI's custom sigmas allow.

steps.title: The kernel's output is within a tolerance declared first of the FP32 attention reference over the shapes Wan, Krea, MOSS and SenseNova use
steps.rationale:
SageAttention2's algorithm (arXiv 2411.10958; SageAttention2++ arXiv 2505.21136; Apache-2.0): Q and K quantised to INT8 per thread with K smoothed by its mean, P and V in FP8 with FP16 accumulation in two levels, written in FlashAttention-2-style mma.sync for sm_89. steps.title: A finished frame is converted on the card to the 8-bit BT.709 YUV 4:2:0 FFmpeg encodes and handed to it as is, so the host reads an eighth of the bytes, keeps no float copy of the frame, and FFmpeg converts nothing
steps.rationale:
Serves: finished clips written faster and in less memory, the effect no longer waiting on the host.

Disappears: four host passes over every finished frame. Today a 3328 x 1920 frame comes back as 77 MB of float32 (finishingEncoder.add: MemcpyDtoH, then a loop rebuilding 19 million float32 values into a second 77 MB slice). The MP4 encoder then converts it value by value through a callback into 19 MB of rgb24, compares it pixel by pixel with bytes.Equal against a 19 MB copy of the frame before, and pipes it to FFmpeg, whose scaler converts it to YUV on the CPU. On rtx-vsr/nvenc's student clip, 81 frames finished at four times, the effect took 3.8 s of a 10.4 s write (7.8 frames a second), so about two thirds of the time is host work. Each stream holds about 197 MB of host buffers.

The fix: the effect already writes 8-bit RGBA on the card. NvCVImage_Transfer converts it there to BT.709 limited-range YUV 4:2:0 (8-bit RGB where the runtime writes no YUV), which is downloaded, 9.6 MB a frame at four times, and piped to FFmpeg as raw yuv420p tagged as clip-encode/colour-709 tags it. The float path stays for unfinished clips. ChangedPixels is counted on the bytes FFmpeg is handed, the change of what it counts named in the record.

Check: TestAFinishedFrameReachesTheEncoderAsEightBitYUV finishes the student clip at four times. The host must read width x height x 3/2 bytes a frame, the decoded frames must be within 40 dB PSNR of the float path's decoded frames, and two writes must be the same bytes. BenchmarkFinishedClipWrite (test-surface/judge-tests) gives frames a second and bytes allocated a frame, before and after, in the landing's message.

Predicted effect: about 16 frames a second at four times (the effect alone runs 21), and about 30 MB of host buffers a stream in place of 197 MB.

steps.title: Qwen2.5-0.5B is trained on a registered objective for a budget of device hours stated before the run, and judged on at least 300 held-out cases against its base by the verdict the store already reconstructs
steps.rationale:
Serves: held-out-quality for a trained model, and the system's purpose as skill.md states it: improvement through its own training, up to a judged candidate.

Disappears: a loop no run has closed. docs/TRAINING_COMPATIBILITY.md holds 26 training claims, 25 of them real-artifact-smoke (a route executes and moves weights, most over 1 to 12 steps), and MOSS's 400 steps move a loss the MOSS document itself says is narrower than better pictures. The one trained-against-base cell on the scorecard is Qwen2.5-0.5B's token accuracy, 0.5167 against 0.5001 on 24 cases. HeldoutGain already says what a gain must clear (two standard errors of the paired differences, internal/evaluation/heldout_verdict.go:271), and 24 cases cannot tell a small gain from none.

Evidence: both reviews of 2026-11-09 name training breadth ahead of its depth as the main gap between what the system is for and what it has shown. The optimizer's one rate rule (P to the -0.6) is held by tests on particular models; a real campaign is its first reading at length, and a run that does not gain is that reading, recorded as a null result with what the detectable gain was.

The model and objective here are the smallest that serve the purpose and are the owner's to change before the run: a person chooses what training starts from. The bar is fixed before the run: gain above the detectable gain on the held-out view, 300 cases or more, one run, no second run for a better result. The device hours are bounded from one measured step before launch.

Predicted effect: held-out-quality of the trained row above its base's by more than its detectable gain, or a recorded null; the base's cells hold.

Batch: device lane.

Evidence limits: 300 cases is a proposed minimum, not a guarantee of power. Fix the detectable effect and uncertainty calculation for independent held-out units before exposure; correlated tokens or questions do not increase the independent sample count. Record an inconclusive or null result without relaxing the bar. Parameter-count learning-rate scaling is a versioned empirical policy for the workloads already measured. If training-side evidence contradicts it, compare a bounded alternative through the existing recipe-bound policy before the held-out judgment; do not tune by repeatedly consulting held-out results or add a second optimizer-policy framework. Keep smoke completion, loss improvement and improved user output as separate claims.

Note: The owner, 2026-11-09: Qwen2.5-0.5B is fine to start from; do not stop to ask. The model and objective are settled for this run.

steps.title: Removing a session folder removes names and never data held elsewhere: a junction or symbolic link in it is never followed and holds the folder, and a file with another name under the models root, the data root or a store is whole after, bytes and read-only attribute both
steps.rationale:
Serves: model, dataset and checkpoint inputs as immutable, under the one new line that deletes beside them. The owner's word of 2026-11-09: be careful not to delete links to data in other places like models.

Disappears: the way 170 GB of weights were lost before, as removeCopy's own comment records (cmd/loop/leftovers.go:1168-1172): a removal that follows a junction out of the folder it is removing. The walk already refuses an entry that holds a link a recursive delete could follow (leftovers.go:236-238) and removeCopy never asks git to remove a directory. This step holds the session line to both, by a test that builds the three cases and reads the linked data after: a directory junction to a models folder, a symbolic link to a model file, and a hard link to one.

Evidence: measured 2026-11-09 in the session folder the next step names: no junction or symbolic link to five levels deep (deeper was not walked), and 15.9 GiB of hard-linked files, the MOSS text encoder and VAE under moss-run/served and moss-run-void/served, four names each, the others in overgo_data/models/MOSS-Image-SFT-797fa8e678b4f and overgo_data/references/moss-image. Removing a hard link's name leaves the other names and the bytes, and frees nothing; the listing says so, giving an entry's bytes apart from the bytes its removal frees.

One thing to read before trusting it: on Windows a file's attributes belong to the file, not the name, so a removal that clears read-only to delete a name clears it on the model's own name too (Qwen3.5-9B-Q8_0.gguf in the models root is read-only). Whether Go's removal does so here is read by the test, and if it does the attribute is put back or the name is removed another way.

steps.title: A session folder is finished only once its session's end is recorded, by a session-end hook or by the end of the process its hold names, and nothing in it is kept by a worktree the helper-copy line holds, an entry named for an open plan row, a committed line or a store registration; a folder whose session's end is unrecorded is reported, never deleted
steps.rationale:
Serves: cleanup as deterministic code, for the largest place it does not yet reach.

Disappears: a line with no end. session-scratch reads "none this command can read", action report (cmd/loop/leftovers.go:160), and sessionFolders answers unknown for every entry (:763-768). One folder shows what that costs: claude/C--Users-jeffm-overgo/9e3511d1-e85c-4667-93c7-a7f762cb886a holds 104.2 GiB of the 107.6, last written 2026-11-08, with 29 of the 51 worktrees git registers under the temporary directory. Its scratchpad holds five copies of the store (store-arm-a to -d and store-copy, 42.5 GiB), moss-run and moss-run-void (35.7 GiB), q9copy (8.9 GiB, a copy of Qwen3.5-9B-Q8_0.gguf) and trained-bf16 (2.8 GiB). 15.9 GiB of moss-run and moss-run-void is hard links to MOSS files in the models root, which a removal frees nothing of and must leave whole there (the step linked-data).

Evidence: the review of 2026-11-09. The rule is the tmp line's (leftovers.go:164, TestTmpEntryBelongsToAnOpenRowOrIsFinished) with one more keeper, the running session: an entry named for an open row is kept, as tmp/<row id>/ is, and a session that wants its probe kept past its end names the folder for its row. Whether a session has ended is read from a signal, never from a folder's age, and only a positive one finishes a folder. The checkout keeps one hold, .overgo-runtime/implementing_session, for the implementing session alone, so its process ending (cmd/loophook, as TestAHoldWhoseProcessEndedIsTaken reads it) speaks for that one session only. Every other running session holds nothing, a review session among them (the session that filed this row wrote it from its own scratch folder while it ran). Reading a missing hold as an ended session would delete a running session's scratch. A session-end hook therefore records each session's end beside the per-session state the checkout keeps, and a folder whose session has neither that record nor an ended hold stays held and is reported. A session that ended before the record existed, such as 9e3511d1, is ended by the lead's own word (cmd/loop -leftovers -end-session <id>, which writes the same record) once read. A worktree is the helper-copy line's to judge first, so nothing uncommitted is deleted by this one.

Reviewed 2026-11-09 by the lead: the end signal is positive only, and an unrecorded end never deletes.

Predicted effect: none on a measured cell.

Batch: host lane.

The copies there now carry no mark. Under this step they stay held, and the listing names them; removing them is the owner's word (the decision stale-data of the data-layout draft names the data root's five).

steps.rationale:
Serves: 2048- and 4096-pixel pictures from MOSS, Krea and SenseNova in about the time of a frame, beside the slower Real-ESRGAN path the plan already holds.

Disappears: nothing.

Evidence: the effect works per frame on a planar RGB image (the binding's own example runs one 960 x 540 frame), so a picture is a one-frame clip. overgo_data/datasets/tifa_v1.0/moss-image-sft holds MOSS's 1024 x 1024 TIFA pictures, which, downscaled by two and four, give pairs with a ground truth. The bar is bicubic, level 0 of the same effect, by the exact paired test at 0.05 on PSNR, and the judge's fidelity questions are asked of a full-size upscale. Where video-finishing/esrgan has landed, Real-ESRGAN is read on the same pairs and the record names which is closer; neither waits for the other.

Predicted effect: a capability overgo lacks for every image generator.
